messages:
maria.g: FYI AuroraHW asked us to run a joint perf/W + throughput benchmark on their upcoming 48GB board. They want a public how-to + marketplace tile. Can we scope a test matrix?
jon.p: Sounds good. My draft matrix: models Llama-2-70B and Llama-3-70B; precisions FP16, INT8, INT4 (if stable); seq lengths 512/1024/2048; batch sizes 1/4/8. Capture tokens/s, p50/p95/p99, and joules/token.
kevin.l: Add GPU temp, power envelope, and sustained-clock checks. Kernel variants: stock, aurora-tuned, and our sparse/vec kernels. Record driver/kernel/build tags.
sara.t: I can own infra + automation. We'll provide a docker image and GH Actions job that runs the sweep and uploads CSVs + telemetry JSON to s3. Need a single run script that emits standardized CSVs.
alex.aurora: Aurora can supply 6 nodes with the 48GB boards and per-rack PDUs. We'll run our power collector locally and share raw CSVs. We'll also provide IPMI access for power sanity checks.
maria.g: Publishing goals: 1) joint technical blog focused on methodology and tuning takeaways, 2) marketplace tile with recommended config and perf profile. Emphasize reproducibility and avoid headline-only claims.
jon.p: Also show single-card and 4-card scaling curves. Include baseline (Redwood default runtime) vs Aurora-tuned kernels. For perf/W, show cold-start vs warmed-KV cache steady-state.
kevin.l: Example run command to standardize:
```
./run_bench --model llama-3-70b \
  --precision int8 \
  --seq 2048 \
  --batch 4 \
  --kernels aurora-tuned,redwood-default \
  --telemetry out/telemetry.json \
  --power /mnt/pdu/power.csv
```
sara.t: I'll wrap that in docker:redwood/bench:aurora-48gb and add a GH Action workflow. Will validate telemetry schema against our bench dashboard.
alex.aurora: We'll provide PDU mapping and a small runbook with NTP and clock sync instructions. If you need kernel artifacts, we can share dkms modules or a prebuilt module tar.
maria.g: Let's create bench/aurora-48gb-joint repo with a publish checklist: raw CSVs, telemetry JSON, container hash, kernel/module hashes, runbook, contacts, and an embargo window field.
marketing.jess: Marketing input: audience is infra/platform engineers. We'll produce explainer slides and short blog visuals. Flag any embargo dates — Aurora likely wants a review window.
jon.p: Action items: 1) infra CI (Sara), 2) runbook & runner script (Maria + Aurora), 3) data ingestion + dashboard (Kevin), 4) blog draft (Marketing), 5) marketplace artifact (Product). Can we assign 2 & 3 now?
sara.t: I'll take infra CI (BENCH-501).
kevin.l: I'll do data ingestion + dashboard (BENCH-502). Metric names I'll standardize: tokens_per_second, joules_per_token, p99_ms, gpu_temp_c, kernel_tag.
maria.g: @alex.aurora can you confirm node access, PDU wires, and on-call support by Monday? Also who will sign the kernel/module NDA if needed?
alex.aurora: Confirmed on nodes and PDU. On-call will be me + engops. We can sign a narrow NDA for kernel bits if required.
benchbot: benchmark-runner: job 9901 started at 1834123600 (sanity run: llama-3-70b, seq=512, batch=1). Artifacts uploading to s3://redwood-bench/aurora-48gb/sanity/9901/
kevin.l: Note: include a small regression test in our eval harness to catch perf drops on future runtime builds. Also tag each run with commit + container digest.
maria.g: Tentative timeline: sanity runs Tue, full sweep Wed-Thu, draft blog next week. Sync in #partnerships Monday 10am PT to confirm resources and landing page copy.
marketing.jess: I'll block the announcement calendar; please add any embargo constraints to the repo checklist.
